passages.text: Do not envy wicked men or desire their company; for their hearts devise violence, and their lips declare trouble.
passages.sermon:
Wicked men do evil things.
Do not envy wicked men.
Do not want to be with wicked men.
Wicked men plan violence in their hearts.
Wicked men speak trouble with their lips.
passages.original: אַל־ תְּ֭קַנֵּא בְּאַנְשֵׁ֣י רָעָ֑ה וְאַל־ תִּתְאָו לִהְי֥וֹת אִתָּֽם׃ כִּי־ שֹׁ֭ד יֶהְגֶּ֣ה לִבָּ֑ם וְ֝עָמָ֗ל שִׂפְתֵיהֶ֥ם תְּדַבֵּֽרְנָה׃

passages.text: By wisdom a house is built and by understanding it is established; through knowledge its rooms are filled with every precious and beautiful treasure.
passages.sermon:
Wisdom builds a house.
Understanding makes the house strong.
Knowledge fills the rooms of the house.
Every room holds precious and beautiful treasures.
passages.original: בְּ֭חָכְמָה יִבָּ֣נֶה בָּ֑יִת וּ֝בִתְבוּנָ֗ה יִתְכּוֹנָֽן׃ וּ֭בְדַעַת חֲדָרִ֣ים יִמָּלְא֑וּ כָּל־ ה֖וֹן יָקָ֣ר וְנָעִֽים׃

passages.text: A wise man is strong, and a man of knowledge enhances his strength.
passages.sermon: A wise man is strong.\r\nA man of knowledge increases his strength.
passages.original: גֶּֽבֶר־ חָכָ֥ם בַּע֑וֹז וְאִֽישׁ־ דַּ֝֗עַת מְאַמֶּץ־ כֹּֽחַ׃

passages.text: Only with sound guidance should you wage war, and victory lies in a multitude of counselors.
passages.sermon:
You must seek wise advice before you go to war.
You should not fight without careful planning.
Many counselors help you find victory.
Good guidance leads to success.
passages.original: כִּ֣י בְ֭תַחְבֻּלוֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה־ לְּךָ֣ מִלְחָמָ֑ה וּ֝תְשׁוּעָ֗ה בְּרֹ֣ב יוֹעֵֽץ׃

passages.text: Wisdom is too high for a fool; he does not open his mouth in the meeting place.
passages.sermon:
A fool cannot reach wisdom.
Wisdom is too high for him.
A fool does not speak in the meeting place.
He keeps his mouth closed at the city gate.
passages.original: רָאמ֣וֹת לֶֽאֱוִ֣יל חָכְמ֑וֹת בַּ֝שַּׁ֗עַר לֹ֣א יִפְתַּח־ פִּֽיהוּ׃

passages.text: He who plots evil will be called a schemer.
passages.sermon: A person who plans to do evil is a schemer.\r\nPeople will call him a schemer.
passages.original: מְחַשֵּׁ֥ב לְהָרֵ֑עַ ל֝֗וֹ בַּֽעַל־ מְזִמּ֥וֹת יִקְרָֽאוּ׃

passages.text: A foolish scheme is sin, and a mocker is detestable to men.
passages.sermon: A foolish scheme is sin.\r\nA mocker is detestable to people.
passages.original: זִמַּ֣ת אִוֶּ֣לֶת חַטָּ֑את וְתוֹעֲבַ֖ת לְאָדָ֣ם לֵֽץ׃

passages.text: If you faint in the day of distress, how small is your strength!
passages.sermon:
A person may face a day of distress.
Distress means trouble or hardship.
If you faint during this time, your strength is small.
Fainting means giving up or losing courage.
Your strength shows in times of trouble.
If you do not stand firm, your strength is weak.
passages.original: הִ֭תְרַפִּיתָ בְּי֥וֹם צָרָ֗ה צַ֣ר כֹּחֶֽכָה׃

passages.text: Rescue those being led away to death, and restrain those stumbling toward the slaughter.
passages.sermon:
Some people are being led away to death.
Some people are stumbling toward slaughter.
Rescue those people.
Hold back those who are stumbling.
Do not withhold your help.
passages.original: הַ֭צֵּל לְקֻחִ֣ים לַמָּ֑וֶת וּמָטִ֥ים לַ֝הֶ֗רֶג אִם־ תַּחְשֽׂוֹךְ׃

passages.text: If you say, “Behold, we did not know about this,” does not He who weighs hearts consider it? Does not the One who guards your life know? Will He not repay a man according to his deeds?
passages.sermon:
God knows every heart.
God understands what is inside each person.
God protects your life.
God knows everything you do.
If you say, “We did not know about this,” God still knows the truth.
God will repay each person for what he has done.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ תֹאמַ֗ר הֵן֮ לֹא־ יָדַ֪עְנ֫וּ זֶ֥ה הֲ‍ֽלֹא־ תֹ֘כֵ֤ן לִבּ֨וֹת׀ הֽוּא־ יָבִ֗ין וְנֹצֵ֣ר נַ֭פְשְׁךָ ה֣וּא יֵדָ֑ע וְהֵשִׁ֖יב לְאָדָ֣ם כְּפָעֳלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Eat honey, my son, for it is good, and the honeycomb is sweet to your taste.
passages.sermon:
A father speaks to his son.
He gives advice.
He says, “Eat honey, my son.”
Honey is good.
The honeycomb is sweet.
It tastes sweet in your mouth.
passages.original: אֱכָל־ בְּנִ֣י דְבַ֣שׁ כִּי־ ט֑וֹב וְנֹ֥פֶת מָ֝ת֗וֹק עַל־ חִכֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Know therefore that wisdom is sweet to your soul. If you find it, there is a future for you, and your hope will never be cut off.
passages.sermon: Wisdom is good for your soul.\r\nIf you find wisdom, you will have a future.\r\nYour hope will not end.
passages.original: כֵּ֤ן׀ דְּעֶ֥ה חָכְמָ֗ה לְנַ֫פְשֶׁ֥ךָ אִם־ מָ֭צָאתָ וְיֵ֣שׁ אַחֲרִ֑ית וְ֝תִקְוָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תִכָּרֵֽת׃פ

passages.text: Do not lie in wait, O wicked man, near the dwelling of the righteous; do not destroy his resting place.
passages.sermon: A wicked person must not wait in secret near the home of a righteous person.\r\nA wicked person must not destroy the resting place of a righteous person.
passages.original: אַל־ תֶּאֱרֹ֣ב רָ֭שָׁע לִנְוֵ֣ה צַדִּ֑יק אַֽל־ תְּשַׁדֵּ֥ד רִבְצוֹ׃

passages.text: For though a righteous man may fall seven times, he still gets up; but the wicked stumble in bad times.
passages.sermon:
A righteous man may fall many times.
He may fall seven times.
He gets up each time.
The wicked stumble in times of trouble.
They do not rise again.
passages.original: כִּ֤י שֶׁ֨בַע׀ יִפּ֣וֹל צַדִּ֣יק וָקָ֑ם וּ֝רְשָׁעִ֗ים יִכָּשְׁל֥וּ בְרָעָֽה׃

passages.text: Do not gloat when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart rejoice when he stumbles, or the LORD will see and disapprove, and turn His wrath away from him.
passages.sermon:
Do not gloat when your enemy falls.
Do not let your heart rejoice when your enemy stumbles.
The LORD sees everything.
The LORD may see your joy over your enemy’s trouble.
This displeases the LORD.
The LORD may turn His wrath away from your enemy.
passages.original: בִּנְפֹ֣ל אוֹיְבֶיךָ אַל־ תִּשְׂמָ֑ח וּ֝בִכָּשְׁל֗וֹ אַל־ יָגֵ֥ל לִבֶּֽךָ׃ פֶּן־ יִרְאֶ֣ה יְ֭הוָה וְרַ֣ע בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְהֵשִׁ֖יב מֵעָלָ֣יו אַפּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Do not fret over evildoers, and do not be envious of the wicked.
passages.sermon:
Evildoers do wrong.
Do not fret over evildoers.
Wicked people act against God.
Do not be envious of the wicked.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּתְחַ֥ר בַּמְּרֵעִ֑ים אַל־ תְּ֝קַנֵּ֗א בָּרְשָׁעִֽים׃

passages.text: For the evil man has no future; the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
passages.sermon:
An evil man has no future.
A wicked person will lose his light.
God will extinguish the lamp of the wicked.
Evil leads to an end with no hope.
passages.original: כִּ֤י׀ לֹֽא־ תִהְיֶ֣ה אַחֲרִ֣ית לָרָ֑ע נֵ֖ר רְשָׁעִ֣ים יִדְעָֽךְ׃

passages.text: My son, fear the LORD and the king, and do not associate with the rebellious.
passages.sermon:
A father speaks to his son.
He gives advice.
He says, "Fear the LORD."
He says, "Fear the king."
He warns his son.
He says, "Do not join with rebellious people."
He says, "Do not associate with those who oppose authority."
passages.original: יְרָֽא־ אֶת־ יְהוָ֣ה בְּנִ֣י וָמֶ֑לֶךְ עִם־ שׁוֹנִ֑ים אַל־ תִּתְעָרָֽב׃

passages.text: For they will bring sudden destruction. Who knows what ruin they can bring?
passages.sermon:
Evil people and rebels can bring disaster.
Their destruction comes suddenly.
No one knows what ruin they can cause.
No one can predict the harm they may bring.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ פִ֭תְאֹם יָק֣וּם אֵידָ֑ם וּפִ֥יד שְׁ֝נֵיהֶ֗ם מִ֣י יוֹדֵֽעַ׃ס

passages.text: These also are sayings of the wise: To show partiality in judgment is not good.
passages.sermon: Wise people say these things.\r\nDo not show favoritism when you judge.\r\nShowing partiality in judgment is not good.
passages.original: גַּם־ אֵ֥לֶּה לַֽחֲכָמִ֑ים הַֽכֵּר־ פָּנִ֖ים בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט בַּל־ טֽוֹב׃

passages.text: Whoever tells the guilty, “You are innocent”— peoples will curse him, and nations will denounce him; but it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and rich blessing will come upon them.
passages.sermon:
This saying comes from the wise.
A person may see someone who is guilty.
He may say to the guilty person, “You are innocent.”
Many peoples will curse this person.
Nations will speak against him.
But some people correct the guilty.
It will go well for those who correct the guilty.
A good blessing will come to them.
passages.original: אֹ֤מֵ֨ר׀ לְרָשָׁע֮ צַדִּ֪יק אָ֥תָּה יִקְּבֻ֥הוּ עַמִּ֑ים יִזְעָמ֥וּהוּ לְאֻמִּֽים׃ וְלַמּוֹכִיחִ֥ים יִנְעָ֑ם וַֽ֝עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם תָּב֥וֹא בִרְכַּת־ טֽוֹב׃

passages.text: An honest answer given is like a kiss on the lips.
passages.sermon:
A wise person values honesty.
An honest answer is good.
An honest answer is pleasant.
An honest answer is like a kiss on the lips.
passages.original: שְׂפָתַ֥יִם יִשָּׁ֑ק מֵ֝שִׁ֗יב דְּבָרִ֥ים נְכֹחִֽים׃

passages.text: Complete your outdoor work and prepare your field; after that, you may build your house.
passages.sermon: Prepare your work outside.\r\nGet your field ready first.\r\nAfter you finish this, build your house.
passages.original: הָ֘כֵ֤ן בַּח֨וּץ׀ מְלַאכְתֶּ֗ךָ וְעַתְּדָ֣הּ בַּשָּׂדֶ֣ה לָ֑ךְ אַ֝חַ֗ר וּבָנִ֥יתָ בֵיתֶֽךָ׃פ

passages.text: Do not testify against your neighbor without cause, and do not deceive with your lips.
passages.sermon:
Do not give false testimony against your neighbor.
Do not speak lies with your mouth.
Only speak truthfully about others.
Do not accuse someone without a good reason.
Do not use your words to mislead people.
passages.original: אַל־ תְּהִ֣י עֵד־ חִנָּ֣ם בְּרֵעֶ֑ךָ וַ֝הֲפִתִּ֗יתָ בִּשְׂפָתֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Do not say, “I will do to him as he has done to me; I will repay the man according to his work.”
passages.sermon:
Do not say, "I will do to him as he did to me."
Do not say, "I will repay the man according to his actions."
Do not seek revenge.
Do not return evil for evil.
passages.original: אַל־ תֹּאמַ֗ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָֽשָׂה־ לִ֭י כֵּ֤ן אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־ לּ֑וֹ אָשִׁ֖יב לָאִ֣ישׁ כְּפָעֳלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: I went past the field of a slacker and by the vineyard of a man lacking judgment.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is Solomon.
Solomon is a wise king of Israel.
Solomon says, “I walked past a field.”
The field belonged to a lazy man.
I also walked past a vineyard.
The vineyard belonged to a man who lacked sense.
passages.original: עַל־ שְׂדֵ֣ה אִישׁ־ עָצֵ֣ל עָבַ֑רְתִּי וְעַל־ כֶּ֝֗רֶם אָדָ֥ם חֲסַר־ לֵֽב׃

passages.text: Thorns had grown up everywhere, thistles had covered the ground, and the stone wall was broken down.
passages.sermon:
I saw a field.
Thorns had grown everywhere in the field.
Thistles covered the ground.
The stone wall around the field was broken down.
passages.original: וְהִנֵּ֨ה עָ֘לָ֤ה כֻלּ֨וֹ׀ קִמְּשֹׂנִ֗ים כָּסּ֣וּ פָנָ֣יו חֲרֻלִּ֑ים וְגֶ֖דֶר אֲבָנָ֣יו נֶהֱרָֽסָה׃

passages.text: I observed and took it to heart; I looked and received instruction: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest, and poverty will come upon you like a robber, and need like a bandit.
passages.sermon:
I am the speaker in this passage.
I saw the field of a lazy man.
I paid close attention to what I saw.
I thought about it deeply.
I learned a lesson from what I saw.
A little sleep brings trouble.
A little slumber brings trouble.
A little folding of the hands to rest brings trouble.
Poverty will come to you suddenly, like a robber.
Need will come to you quickly, like an armed man.
passages.original: וָֽאֶחֱזֶ֣ה אָ֭נֹכִֽי אָשִׁ֣ית לִבִּ֑י רָ֝אִ֗יתִי לָקַ֥חְתִּי מוּסָֽר׃ מְעַ֣ט שֵׁ֭נוֹת מְעַ֣ט תְּנוּמ֑וֹת מְעַ֓ט׀ חִבֻּ֖ק יָדַ֣יִם לִשְׁכָּֽב׃ וּבָֽא־ מִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ רֵישֶׁ֑ךָ וּ֝מַחְסֹרֶ֗יךָ כְּאִ֣ישׁ מָגֵֽן׃פ
